inline_comments.comment:
The formula `(index % MAX_SECTIONS) - 1` is incorrect due to a parenthesization error. With `MAX_SECTIONS = 12`:
- `index = 0` (first child): `(0 % 12) - 1 = -1` — the first level-2 node gets `section = -1`, producing CSS class `section--1`, which collides with the root node's own special class.
- `index = 12` (13th child): `(12 % 12) - 1 = -1` — same invalid result again.

The test expectations in this very PR (child1 → 0, child11 → 10, child12 → 0, child13 → 1, …) are consistent with `index % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1)` (i.e., `index % 11`), not with `(index % MAX_SECTIONS) - 1`. With the formula as written, every new test assertion would fail. The intended expression should be `index % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1)` — note the parentheses around `MAX_SECTIONS - 1`, not around `index % MAX_SECTIONS`.

This import creates a circular dependency: `mindmapDb.ts` now imports `MAX_SECTIONS` from `svgDraw.ts`, while `svgDraw.ts` already imports `import type { MindmapDB } from './mindmapDb.js'`. TypeScript's type-only import on the `svgDraw.ts` side prevents a runtime cycle, but the layering violation remains: a data-model/database module should not depend on a rendering/SVG module. Consider extracting `MAX_SECTIONS` (and potentially other shared constants) into `mindmapTypes.ts` or a new `mindmapConstants.ts` file so both `mindmapDb.ts` and `svgDraw.ts` can import from it without a circular relationship.

`MAX_SECTIONS = 12` implies 12 usable sections, but both the existing `drawNode` (line 186: `fullSection % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1)`) and the new `assignSections` formula use `MAX_SECTIONS - 1 = 11` as the actual modulus, meaning only sections 0–10 are ever assigned — section 11 is never used. The constant's name and value are misleading. Consider either renaming it to `NUM_SECTION_COLORS` (set to 11) to accurately reflect the number of usable sections, or at minimum adding a comment explaining why the off-by-one exists.

The test checks child1 (index 0) and then jumps to child11 (index 10), skipping all intermediate indices. Adding a spot-check for a middle value (e.g., child6 at index 5, expecting `section = 5`) would confirm the non-wrapping range still behaves correctly and isn't accidentally affected by the modulo operation.

child11 (index 10) is the last node before wrapping begins — it's the boundary case — but its `cssClasses` are not asserted. Adding `expect(child11.cssClasses).toBe('mindmap-node section-10')` alongside the existing section-value check would mirror the cssClasses assertions done for child12–15 and confirm the boundary is handled correctly end-to-end.

general_comments.comment: The core formula fix and the new test are internally inconsistent: the test expectations precisely match `index % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1)` but the implementation uses `(index % MAX_SECTIONS) - 1`. These two expressions differ in both operator precedence and behavior (the latter produces -1 for the first child and for every 12th child). The tests as written would fail against the code as written. The formula needs to be corrected to `index % (MAX_SECTIONS - 1)` for the fix to actually work.
